newsitem.title: THAILAND: TelecomAsia sees losses until 1997 H2.
newsitem.headline: TelecomAsia sees losses until 1997 H2.

text.p: Thai telecommunications company TelecomAsia Plc expects a poor fourth quarter and is likely to post losses until the second half of 1997, the company's vice chairman Vallobh Vimolvanich said on Thursday.

"We will definitely still be in the red this quarter ... it should be about the same as the last quarter or maybe a little worse," he said. "Towards the end of 1997 or even a little before it will turn around. Looking at the TA group in general, something which has been posting big losses is UTV, and UTV is turning around."

UTV is TelecomAsia's cable television network provider and programme making subsidiary. Vallobh said UTV now had 90,000 paying households, and the company was signing up 20,000 new subscribers per month.
He said UTV was expected to break even by the middle of 1997 by which time it would have separated its network and its programme making arms.
TelecomAsia reported losses in the third quater of 1996 at 420.4 million baht ($16.81 million).
Vallobh ruled out any sale in the short term of TelecomAsia's approximate 14 percent of APT Satellite Holdings, which is due to list next week in Hong Kong.
"I think the future of APT is quite bright and we will definitely hold on to our stake for as long as possible," he said.

Vallobh said losses were also linked to the company having install 2.6 million fixed telephone lines faster than expected and lower connection rates than forecast. The company received the concession from the government to install the lines.
He said a slump in Bangkok property had stalled a number of connections in office developments which had bought large numbers of TelecomAsia lines.

"If we look at the active lines it is similar to our expected revenues and even higher than we expected on business lines. However we are still not happy with the percentage of idle lines," Vallobh said.
He said the company had connected more than one million lines, out of the 2.6 million it had installed.

With the blessing of the state controlling body, the Telephone Organisation of Thailand, Vallobh said TelecomAsia may try to overcome network congestion problems by connecting pager and mobile suppliers directly with its network.
He said plans for the introduction of the company's limited cordless roaming phone system were on schedule for the second half of next year.
As far as international interests are concerned Vallobh ruled out TelecomAsia's return to the Indian market, from which it withdrew earlier this year, given political uncertainty.
"How can you hope to do business there when you don't know if the new government is going to honour agreements reached under previous ones," he said.
